ratings.concept: (n+l) rule for orbital energies: 3s (3) < 3p (4) < 4s (4, higher n breaks the tie) < 3d (5), which is why 4s fills before 3d
ratings.strategy_evidence: Within one shell energy rises with l, so 3s must come before 3p; that single fact strikes options 3 (3s 4s 3p 3d) and 4 (4s 3s 3p 3d), which both interpose 4s before 3p.

traps.label: sequence_endpoint_or_adjacency
traps.route: keeps 3s < 3p and swaps the single final adjacency to "3d 4s", which is the order given by the principal quantum number alone instead of by (n+l)

traps.label: no_derivation_route
traps.route: no filling rule reaches 3s 4s 3p 3d: by (n+l) the values are 3s = 3, 3p = 4, 4s = 4, 3d = 5, and the tie between 3p and 4s is broken in favour of the lower n, so 4s can never precede 3p; by n alone 4s is last. The option widens the spread

traps.label: no_derivation_route
traps.route: no filling rule reaches 4s 3s 3p 3d either: 4s has (n+l) = 4 against 3s's 3, so it cannot be lowest on (n+l), and it is highest on n alone

ratings.reason: This question requires applying the (n+l) rule to four named orbitals, demonstrated by the key order "3s 3p 4s 3d", in which 4s (n+l = 4) precedes 3d (n+l = 5).
